$comment: HZ-134. Input/expected pairs for the work-item field bindings, asserted by BOTH server/test/domain-fields-cases.test.mjs and farm/tests/test_fields_fixtures.py. The `shared` section is the point of the file: domain/js/fields.js and domain/py/fields.py are two independent hand-written implementations, and without this nothing would prove a field lookup, a patch-limit derivation or a validation rule meant the same thing in both languages — the exact gap domain/fixtures/lifecycle-cases.json was added to close for the step table. Every case in `shared` runs in both suites, and each suite asserts it executed the exact ids listed in shared.manifest, so a suite cannot quietly skip a section and still pass. The `js` and `py` sections cover the helpers that exist in only one binding; a coverage guard in each suite asserts SET EQUALITY between that section's keys and the binding's real exports, so a new export with no case fails, and a stale case naming a removed export fails too. Every field name in this file is FABRICATED on purpose — no real work-item field or limit appears, so the fixture is not a second declaration of the table.
